children: Shares of J.Jill gained after the company guided for sales to potentially grow this year as its turnaround plan gains steam.
The stock climbed 13% to $22.50 in premarket trading on Wednesday. Shares were up 45% year to date at market close.
For the full year, J.Jill now forecasts sales to be flat to up 2%, compared with its prior guidance for flat to down 2%.
For the third quarter, J.Jill guided for sales to be up 3% to 5%. Analysts polled by FactSet were looking for sales of $152.5 million, or up about 1.3% year over year.
The company said its outlook includes net tariff refunds, as well as steps it will take to reinvest those refunds in marketing.
The updated guidance comes as J.Jill posted higher profit and an uptick in revenue in the latest quarter.

Chief Executive Mary Ellen Coyne said the results show progress across the company's priorities, including efforts to improve its product assortment and customer journey. The company's customer base is stabilizing, and growth in new customers is ramping up, she said.

"While we are still in the early stages of this evolution, we are pleased with our momentum and are strategically investing in the business to position J.Jill for sustainable, long-term growth," Coyne said.
The company posted a second-quarter profit of $16.8 million, or $1.11 a share, compared with $10.5 million, or 69 cents a share, a year earlier.
Adjusted earnings per share, which include a boost from tariff refunds, were $1.24. Analysts expected 57 cents a share.
The company said it received $13.3 million in net tariff refunds in the quarter.
Revenue ticked up 0.5% to $154.8 million, topping analyst estimates of $151.3 million.
